metadata.processing_notes: Comprehensive extraction from 75 colony/territory files, including geographic entities, people with titles/salaries/honors, institutions, economic data, infrastructure, demographics, and historical events. Historical spelling preserved throughout.

places.name: Antigua
places.description: Island in the Caribbean Sea, about 54 miles in circumference. Dependencies include Barbuda (62 square miles) and Redonda (1 mile by 1/4 mile). Main town: St. John's (population 9,047 in 1909).

places.name: Barbuda
places.description: Dependency of Antigua, lying 25 miles due north. Very flat with large lagoon on west side. Population 775. Produces salt, phosphates of lime, suitable for cattle grazing and horse rearing.

places.name: Redonda
places.description: Small island between Montserrat and Nevis. 1,000 feet high. Valuable for phosphate of alumina mines. Annual export approximately 7,000 tons. Employs 90 men.

places.name: Bermuda
places.description: Island colony in North Atlantic. Contains St. George's parish and other parishes including Hamilton, Sandy's, Pembroke, Devonshire, Paget, Warwick, and Southampton.

places.name: Jamaica
places.description: Largest of British West Indies. 144 miles in length, 50 miles in extreme breadth. Mountainous with main ridge running east-west. Capital: Kingston (population 48,504 in 1891) with fine harbour. Contains 2,692,480 acres total.

places.name: Kingston
places.description: Capital of Jamaica, situated on south coast. Population 48,504 in 1891. Fine harbour. Major port serving island exports.

places.name: Montego Bay
places.description: Major town in Jamaica, parish of Saint James. Population 4,651 in census. Port of registry.

places.name: Mauritius
places.description: Island in Indian Ocean, 115 miles from Réunion, 934 miles from Seychelles, 1,300 miles from Natal. Extreme length 36 miles N-S, breadth 28 miles E-W. Volcanic formation surrounded by coral reefs.

places.name: Port Louis
places.description: Capital and chief town of Mauritius. Population 52,740 (with suburbs) in 1901 census. Seat of government. One of best harbours in East, with capacity for 100+ vessels. Defended by Fort Adelaide (citadel) and Fort George. Contains large barracks and military stores.

places.name: Curepipe
places.description: Second largest town of Mauritius, incorporated 1890. Population 13,296 (1901 census). Located on uplands in Plaines Wilhems district. Temperate climate; many families reside in villas during summer season.

places.name: Fiji
places.description: Colony comprising islands between 15° and 22° S latitude, 177° W to 175° E longitude. Includes 200-250 islands, rocks, and reefs. Principal islands: Viti Levu (4,112 sq mi), Vanua Levu (2,432 sq mi), Tavuni (217 sq mi), Kadavu (124 sq mi).

places.name: Suva
places.description: Capital of Fiji, located on south coast of Viti Levu with fine harbour. Population 1,112 (white population) at 1906 census. Seat of government transferred from Levuka in 1882.

places.name: Ceylon
places.description: Island in Indian Ocean off southern extremity of Hindustán. Ancient Taprobane. Extreme length 266 miles N-S (Point Palmyra to Dondra Head), greatest width 140.5 miles E-W. Area equal to Holland and Belgium.

places.name: Hong Kong
places.description: Island colony off south-eastern coast of China at mouth of Canton River, 40 miles east of Macao, 91 miles south of Canton. Irregular ridge stretching E-W. Main island peaks rise nearly 2,000 feet. Length 11 miles, breadth 2-5 miles.

places.name: Victoria
places.description: City of Hong Kong, extends for 4 miles at base of hills protecting south side of harbour. Population 336,488 with suburbs. Built on slope of hills facing sea. Contains new buildings on Praya West Reclamation (completed 1903).

places.name: Kowloon
places.description: Opposite peninsula ceded to Great Britain by Treaty entered into by Lord Elgin in 1861. Now forms part of Hong Kong Colony. Also includes leased territory (370 square miles) for 99 years from 1898, including Mira Bay and Deep Bay.

places.name: Malta
places.description: Group of islands in Mediterranean Sea, 58 miles from Sicily, 80 miles from Syracuse, 142 from Reggio, 130 from mainland Africa. Malta length 17 miles x 9 miles breadth. Includes Gozo (24.804 sq mi), Comino (1 sq mi), and small islets.

places.name: Valletta
places.description: Chief town and capital of Malta. Population 40,406 with suburbs (Floriana, Sliema, St. Julian's) in 1901. The Three Cities (Senglea, Cospicua, Vittoriosa) population 17,492. Citta Vecchia (old capital) population 9,067 with suburbs.

places.name: Gibraltar
places.description: Narrow peninsula on south-west coast of Spain. Consists of high mountain 'The Rock' (1,439 feet maximum elevation) and flat sandy North Front. Length 2.5 miles, greatest breadth 0.25 miles.

places.name: British Guiana
places.description: Colony in South America. Population estimate 305,090 (31 December 1909). Made up of diverse population: Aborigines, East Indians, Chinese, Portuguese, Africans, Europeans, and Blacks.

infrastructure.name: Jamaica Telegraph System
infrastructure.description: Connecting all principal towns. Total mileage: 375.5 miles along roads, 137 miles P.O. lines on railway, 184.5 miles along railway lines. Total cost approximately 20,324£. Receipts 1908-9: 6,220£ 17s. 9d.

infrastructure.name: Jamaica Road System
infrastructure.description: System of main roads. Condition favourable compared to European roads. Also approximately 4,318 miles of parochial roads.

infrastructure.name: North Line
infrastructure.description: Railway line from Port Louis to sea coast village, approximately parallel to northern coast line.

infrastructure.name: Midland Line
infrastructure.description: Running across island to sea coast town Mahébourg. Gradient in many places 1 in 27.

infrastructure.name: Fiji Island Harbours
infrastructure.description: Fiji rich in harbours and roadsteads. Each island surrounded by barrier reef, accessible through passages usually opposite considerable valleys/rivers. Ships lie safely at anchor protected by natural breakwater.

infrastructure.name: Victoria Harbour
infrastructure.description: One of most magnificent harbours in world. Granite hills surrounding rise 2,000-3,000 feet high. Contains three graving docks.

infrastructure.name: Malta Railway
infrastructure.description: Originally built by Malta Railway Company at cost of 100,000£. Became property of Local Government in 1890.

infrastructure.name: Electric Tramway and Motor-Omnibus Service
infrastructure.description: Connecting principal towns and villages with Valletta. Also telephone exchange with 742 miles of wires.

infrastructure.name: Eastern Telegraph Company Station
infrastructure.description: Direct cables to: Alexandria (3), Gibraltar (3), Bone (2), Messina (1), Tripoli (1), Sicily (1), Zante (1).

demographics.description: Only 2% white; remainder chiefly African descent; about 14,000 imported coolies; about 481 Chinese (1897). Four-fifths of population pure negroes.

events.description: Legislative Council passed Act abrogating itself and substituting Crown Colony system. New Council of 16 members (8 official, 8 non-official) all nominated by Governor.
Ordinance No. 7 of 1910 limited duration of Legislative Council to three years.

Kingston devastated by terrible earthquake causing great loss of life and immense destruction of property. Mansion House Fund opened. Parliament voted free grant of £150,000 and authorised loan of £800,000 for relief and rebuilding.
Two buildings completed: General Post Office and Treasury, and King's House (official residence of Governor). Law Courts being built.
Slave Trade abolished. At this time 323,827 slaves in Jamaica. During last 8 years of trade, 80,821 slaves were imported.
Abolition of slavery. Jamaica received £6,161,927 of £20,000,000 granted by Imperial Government as compensation to slave-owners.
Island discovered by Portuguese navigator Pedro Mascarenhas. Portuguese used as port of call, no settlement made.
Dutch fleet landed on island. Admiral J. C. Van Neck gave the name Mauritius in honour of Stadtholder Prince Maurice of Nassau.
Party of Frenchmen landed in Mauritius. In 1721 formally taken possession by French on behalf of French East India Company; later in 1767 on behalf of Crown of France.
Island surrendered to Great Britain after expeditionary force from India and several naval engagements. Laws, religion, and customs of inhabitants guaranteed in capitulation instrument.
Treaty of Paris confirmed British possession of island.
Terrible hurricane visited island causing enormous destruction of buildings and crops.
Part of town of Port Louis entirely destroyed by fire.
During small cyclone, railway train blown down in ravine at Pailles Bridge. Five persons killed and great loss of material sustained.
Islands discovered by Tasman.
Islands visited by Captain Cook.
Captain Bligh on launch of Bounty sighted part of group, chased by canoe from island of Waya.
Missionaries settled in Fiji and met with great success.
Sovereignty of islands ceded to Her Majesty by Thakombau (Chief of Bau), Maafu (Chief of Lau Confederacy), and other principal chiefs.
Council of Government appointed by Letters Patent under Great Seal.

Letters Patent and Instructions issued, and Ordinance passed in Ceylon settled present constitution. Legislative Council now has 21 members including ex-officio members, Government Agents for provinces, Chief Civil Medical Officer, and six nominated and four elected unofficial members.
Colony, then desolate island sparsely inhabited by fishermen, ceded to Great Britain.
Cession confirmed by Treaty of Nankin.
Charter granted for Hong Kong.
Discovery of gold in Australia led to increased Chinese emigration and Hong Kong became of much commercial importance.
Opening of Suez Canal greatly increased Hong Kong's trade.
Earliest known inhabitants were Phoenicians who left traces in famous temples of Hagar Kine in Malta and Torre dei Giganti in Gozo.

Grand Master Hompesch capitulated without resistance to Napoleon Bonaparte, who dispersed the Order of St. John. Maltese rose against French. British fleet blockaded French for two years. French surrendered to British in 1800.
Islands finally annexed to British Crown by Treaty of Paris.
Rock captured by British forces under Sir George Rooke.
Gibraltar ceded by Treaty of Utrecht.
Great siege successfully defended by Gen. Eliot (afterwards Lord Heathfield).
Churches and religious denominations were all endowed under temporary Act; grants expired in 1908.
